item.title: American Express faces $350 million penalty from OCC over AML failures
item.description:
On Thursday, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Federal Reserve Board issued enforcement actions against American Express, levying a $350 million civil money penalty on its bank subsidiary. The OCC also cited systemic breakdowns in suspicious activity monitoring that allowed roughly $13 billion of suspected money laundering to flow through the card network over the past decade.
The Fed issued a separate cease-and-desist order to American Express and its travel‑related services arm. An Amex regulatory filing noted that part of the penalty had been reserved in prior periods and would not affect its full‑year 2026 guidance. The filing added that the consent orders are not expected to alter the company’s 2027 outlook, and an Amex spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The OCC stressed that institutions of American Express’s scale need to devote sufficient resources to AML compliance to safeguard economic and national security.
“The OCC expects banks of American Express’s size and complexity to devote sufficient resources to ensure compliance with laws and regulations designed to detect and prevent money laundering, which are critical to both economic and national security,” Jonathan Gould, Comptroller of the Currency said.
Source: Payments Dive (https://paymentsdive.com/news/amex-dinged-by-fed-occ-must-pay-350m-for-aml-failures/832575)

item.title: FedEx and Stripe plan 2027 financing product using supply-chain data for SMBs
item.description:
FedEx and Stripe announced a financing product slated for 2027 that will incorporate FedEx supply-chain intelligence—such as shipment activity, inventory movement and fulfillment performance—into Stripe Capital’s underwriting for FedEx SMB customers. PYMNTS Intelligence found that 57% of financial institutions cite inaccurate or incomplete SMB records as a key underwriting obstacle, while half of SMBs depend on day-to-day sales proceeds or cash reserves to stay operational.
The product will blend shipment volume, inventory turns and fulfillment speed with traditional credit scores and bank statements in Stripe Capital’s risk models. According to PYMNTS, digital channels accounted for 57% of SMB sales on average last year, creating a growing trail of order and stock data that lenders can now tap. Only 44% of small businesses reported having access to financing or working-capital solutions, a gap the new data‑driven approach aims to narrow.
Lenders have repeatedly warned that small‑business financial records are often inaccurate, outdated or incomplete, making underwriting risky. Supply‑chain data, which tracks orders, warehouse moves and shipments, captures physical commerce that is increasingly recorded in digital systems.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/smbs/2026/supply-chain-data-moves-into-smb-underwriting)

item.title: Amazon Prime Big Deal Days generate $9.86 billion in U.S. online sales
item.description:
Amazon Prime Big Deal Days on Oct. 6 and 7, 2026 drove $9.86 billion in U.S. online sales, according to Adobe. Online sales during the event rose 8.5% year over year, up from $9.09 billion in the 2025 Prime Big Deal Days.
Adobe’s data came from direct online transactions, covering more than 1 trillion visits to U.S. retail sites, 100 million SKUs and 18 product categories. More than 200 of the Top 2000 largest online retailers used Adobe for web analytics in 2025, together accounting for over $836 billion in ecommerce sales that year. Mobile devices accounted for 52.0% of online sales during the event, roughly $5.1 billion, while buy now, pay later services powered 6.0% of orders, representing $692.3 million in spending. Discounts peaked at 20% off list price, with electronics sales up 85%, toy sales up 158%, video game sales up 90%, personal care up 73%, and costume sales up 610% compared to September 2026 levels.
The event previously took place on Oct. 7 and 8, 2025, when U.S. online sales reached $9.09 billion, a 7.3% year‑over‑year increase. Both iterations fell on a Tuesday and Wednesday, and the 2026 edition recorded higher spending than the 2025 edition.
Source: Digital Commerce 360 (https://digitalcommerce360.com/2026/10/08/amazon-prime-day-big-deal-days-sales-2026)

item.title: WooCommerce launches version 11.2 with checkout date picker and sticky filters
item.description:
WooCommerce has released version 11.2. Stores with up to 50,000 products can now reorder items faster and see reduced database queries when pulling reports.
Sticky positioning can be enabled for the Product Filters block, keeping filters on screen as shoppers scroll through long category pages. Quantity selectors, product images, and filter chips now offer new style controls such as borders, shadows, colors, rounded corners, font, and spacing adjustments. Account emails for password reset, new account, and confirmation no longer CC or BCC the store owner, because those messages now contain login links meant only for the customer. Standard download links remain functional, while a rare custom or imported link containing malformed data may fail and can be reissued from the order when a customer reports an issue. Shop managers can no longer edit users who also hold roles like forum or membership, so WP Admin must handle those role updates. WooCommerce 11.2 delivers security improvements and a database update, advising merchants to back up before applying the update. The product CSV importer now matches rows by global unique ID, then SKU, then GTIN, UPC, EAN, or ISBN when updating existing products. Merchants using the Checkout block can add a date field for shoppers to pick a preferred delivery date or birthday, with limits set via a short code snippet. Store owners selling to EU customers can now configure both the acknowledgment and notification emails for order withdrawals, editing messages, choosing recipients, or turning either email off. Catalog and admin screens load faster, with variable products checking out quicker and report totals using fewer database queries that no longer grow with customer count.
Source: WooCommerce Blog (https://woocommerce.com/posts/woocommerce-11-2)

item.title: Natura launches $99 Interface ring for 24/7 AI agent control
item.description:
Natura launches its Interface ring, a $99 wearable that lets users command AI agents and track health, according to a TechCrunch report dated Oct. 8. The always‑on ring is meant to give users round‑the‑clock access to AI agents for tasks such as tracking workouts, checking schedules, reordering shampoo, or turning off a TV.
Priced at $99, the Interface ring is water‑resistant enough to wear while showering or sleeping, and it connects to a smartphone app that relays voice commands to the AI agents. Users can invoke agents to perform actions like ordering products, managing loyalty programs, or setting alarms, with the ring capturing speech via a built‑in microphone. The ring does not store payment credentials locally; instead, it relies on the user’s existing wallet or card network for any transactions initiated by the agent. Natura claims the ring’s applications are limitless, citing examples such as tracking a run, checking a morning schedule, ordering shampoo mid‑shower, or turning off a TV and setting an alarm.
“Over time, we evolved to an understanding where you really want to have access to your agents 24/7,” Carlo Edoardo Ferraris said.
After years of developing consumer hardware, founder Carlo Edoardo Ferraris sought a new interface that would let users interact with AI agents as naturally as speaking to another person. The Interface ring was first disclosed in a TechCrunch report on Oct. 8, which described the device as a health‑tracking wearable that also enables AI agent control.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/artificial-intelligence/2026/natura-wants-people-controlling-ai-agents-from-their-fingers)

item.title: FMCSA advances split‑sleeper berth pilot with 256‑driver trial
item.description:
The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration moved closer to launching a split‑sleeper berth pilot that could allow up to 256 drivers to test flexible off‑duty splits. Participants would receive $1,600 each and could try 5‑5 or 6‑4 sleeper‑berth splits if the minimum berth period falls from seven to five hours.
The pilot would enroll up to 256 commercial motor vehicle drivers who would record how they split their required 10 hours off duty each day for 16 weeks. Participants would receive a flat $1,600 stipend for completing the study, as noted in a Department of Transportation press release from late August. During the trial they could choose any split of sleeper berth time, including the proposed 5‑5 or 6‑4 arrangements, if the minimum berth period is lowered from seven to five hours. Comments on the information collection plan are being accepted until December 7, after a Federal Register notice issued Wednesday opened the process. The effort follows a September 2025 notice that first sought comment on changing the split sleeper berth rule and an April 2025 executive order directing the Secretary of Transportation to improve truck drivers’ working conditions. Earlier work on the idea dates to a 2013 joint submission by the American Trucking Associations and the Minnesota Trucking Association, after FMCSA listening sessions in 2010 and the 2011 Hours of Service rule that excluded splits beyond 7‑3. Under the existing hours‑of‑service rule, drivers may split their 10 hours off duty only as a 7‑hour sleeper berth period plus a 2‑hour period, or the reverse 8‑2 split.
“The notice published Wednesday requests comments on the information collection the FMCSA will seek through the pilot,” Chris Eckhart, partner at the trucking‑focused Scopelitis law firm said.
The September 2025 Federal Register notice described the proposal as a notification of proposed pilot program and request for comments on split sleeper berth flexibility. It built on an April 2025 executive o
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/fmcsa-split-sleeper-berth-pilot-program-moves-closer-to-launch)

item.title: FMCSA grants five-year beacon exemption for Level 4 autonomous trucks
item.description:
The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration approved a five-year exemption that permits carriers operating Level 4 autonomous trucks to replace reflective warning triangles with cab‑mounted amber beacons, valid through October 7, 2031. The ruling supersedes Aurora’s earlier series of four three‑month waivers and is available to any Level 4 carrier that notifies FMCSA before operation.
Each beacon must be amber, satisfy SAE J595 Class 1 photometric standards and be mounted at least 100 inches above the ground, level with or higher than the side mirrors. The lights must switch on within five minutes of a stop and continue flashing together with the hazard flashers until the vehicle moves again or is recovered. Operation is limited to roads within the carrier’s validated operational design domain; hazardous‑material, passenger, double‑trailer beyond two 28‑foot units, triple‑trailer and tanker‑only restrictions apply as outlined. All carriers except Aurora must email FMCSA beforehand, certify under penalty of perjury that they have the beacons and will comply, and must report any crash involving the beacons within five calendar days and file annual malfunction reports by November 1.
“Going from a temporary waiver to a five-year exemption gives the industry a lot of confidence,” Jeff Farrah, CEO of the Autonomous Vehicle Industry Association said.
“will give the autonomous freight industry a key piece of regulatory certainty that will allow us to continue to scale safely,” Bart Teeter, director of fleet and operational safety at Bot Auto said.
FMCSA had denied Aurora and Waymo’s 2023 request for the same relief in December 2024, citing insufficient specificity. After the denial, the agency issued Aurora a narrow waiver from October 10, 2025 through January 9, 2026, during which the company ran beacons on 34 trucks that logged more than 500,000 miles.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/fmcsa-aurora-warning-beacon-exemption-five-year)

item.title: Global container volumes hit record 17.46 million TEUs in August
item.description:
Container Trades Statistics reported that global container shipping volumes reached a record 17.46 million twenty-foot equivalent units in August in its Oct. 8 report. August liftings were 3.7% higher than in August 2025, pushing year‑to‑date volumes up 4.7% year‑over‑year compared with the same period last year.
The CTS Global Price Index rose two points to 117 in August, its highest level since July 2024, while overall North American container imports were up 2% through August versus the same period last year and Sub‑Saharan Africa imports grew 13% through August. The combined Indian Sub‑Continent and Middle East region saw imports fall 5% and exports drop 10% year‑to‑date, while steady Asia exports increased 8% year‑to‑date, adding roughly 6.3 million TEUs and trans‑Pacific trade rose 5% year‑to‑date. August volumes were 7.2% higher than in August 2024 and 12.9% above August 2023 levels. The Global Price Index was about 50% above its January level and 44% higher than in August 2025, and CTS warned that slowing month‑to‑month growth could signal a moderation in demand heading into the final quarter.
The previous record was set in July 2026. Earlier in 2026, North American imports had posted negative year‑to‑date growth before a gradual recovery began in May.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/global-container-volumes-hit-record-17-46-million-teus)

item.title: Google Cloud offers Gemini agent for enterprise Workspace users
item.description:
Google Cloud launched a universal Gemini agent for enterprise Workspace users that runs in Gmail, Drive, Docs, and Calendar. It can respond to queries, perform knowledge tasks, generate images and media, and write and execute code.
It is secured through identity and policy management, authorization and permission controls, and secure sandboxing and network gateways, and includes cost controls via multi-model orchestration, Smart Routing, and real-time spend caps. The agent can securely connect to a user’s company software and any Model Context Protocol server, use custom skills added by the user, and learn from each interaction. Industry‑specific agents for financial services and legal are now in preview, with government, healthcare, and retail versions planned for release soon.
In April, Google Cloud unveiled the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform as a unified system for building, connecting, securing, and governing AI agents. In August it said it had agentic AI solutions for financial services and legal in preview, positioning them as the first in a series of industry‑specific offerings.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/artificial-intelligence/2026/google-cloud-targets-enterprise-market-with-universal-agent-work)

item.title: Bond-eye, Maxxam and Woolmark launch 45/45/10 wool-blend swimwear fabric
item.description:
Bond-eye, Maxxam and Woolmark have launched a swimwear fabric made of 45% Australian Merino wool, 45% Tencel and 10% elastane. The fabric debuts as part of a 26‑piece collection designed to cut reliance on nylon and polyester.
The material resulted from a two‑year collaborative development process assisted by a specialist Italian knitting mill. It builds on Bond‑eye’s ten‑year partnership with Rosemary Moore, the founder of Maxxam, who first introduced tubular crinkle fabric over four decades ago. Woolmark subjected the fabric to strict performance testing to ensure colourfastness in chlorinated pool water and seawater. The four‑way stretch construction lets garments adjust to sizes from extra‑small to large without losing shape or luxurious feel. The blend uses wool’s natural elasticity, temperature regulation and moisture‑managing abilities to provide a soft, breathable feel suitable for active swimwear.
“The challenge was not simply to introduce wool into swimwear, but to develop a fabrication that could meet the category’s technical demands without compromising the qualities that make Merino wool distinctive,” Bryan Fry, managing director of Woolmark said.
“It’s exciting to use wool because of its natural elasticity and recovery, as well as its moisture‑wicking and temperature‑regulating properties—we wanted to explore how those qualities could translate into swimwear,” Mim Goode, Bond-eye designer said.
Bond-eye has worked with Rosemary Moore for more than a decade on tubular crinkle fabric, which Moore originally invented over forty years ago. Maxxam, founded by Moore, continues to develop the crinkle technology while Woolmark provides certification and technical support for natural‑fiber innovations.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/sustainability/bond-eye-maxxam-and-woolmark-launch-wool-blend-swimwear-1239333060)

item.title: Mastercard and SoFi enable Orbi to launch crypto‑linked debit card in Mexico
item.description:
Mastercard and SoFi are helping Orbi launch a crypto‑linked debit card in Mexico, where stablecoins made up 40% of crypto purchases in 2025. The card lets users spend either fiat or crypto balances at checkout while merchants receive traditional fiat, and SoFi supplies the BIN sponsorship, issuance, authorization, processing and compliance infrastructure. The program is available to Orbi customers across Mexico and does not require merchants to alter their existing point‑of‑sale systems.
SoFi’s role includes providing the bank identification number, handling transaction approvals, and ensuring compliance with local regulations.
“Mexico is one of the world’s largest remittance markets, and stablecoins are becoming an increasingly important way to move money across its borders,” Kathleen Pierce-Gilmore, SoFi Tech Solutions President said.
In 2025, stablecoins accounted for 40% of crypto purchases among Bitso users in Mexico, Argentina, Brazil and Colombia, surpassing bitcoin’s 18% share. A PYMNTS Intelligence report released in July found that consumers are interested in using crypto for purchases but face acceptance, trust and uneven payment experiences, noting that linked cards could help bridge the gap.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/cryptocurrency/2026/mastercard-sofi-help-orbi-launch-crypto-card-mexico)

item.title: Meta unveils AI‑enhanced ad tools and Shopify checkout at Advertising Week
item.description:
Meta announced a suite of AI‑powered advertising updates and new direct‑checkout features at its Advertising Week presentation in New York today. The updates give the business assistant more memory and agentic functions, expand Ads Creative Studio to additional advertisers, and enable Shopify buyers to complete purchases without leaving Messenger.
The business assistant now incorporates creative insights, retains context from prior quarters, and can generate creative assets, adjust targeting, or modify budgets via conversational prompts. Meta is also testing importing tools that let brands upload their strategy and brand‑voice guidelines to further refine the assistant’s outputs. Agentic capabilities added to the assistant allow it to create ad elements, change audience targeting, and alter an ad’sbudget through natural‑language commands. Scheduled tasks such as recurring performance reports and alerts are being tested to keep advertisers informed of potential issues. Ads Creative Studio, which uses performance data and audience insights to highlight what’s working in campaigns, is being rolled out beyond selected ad partners to a broader set of brands. The studio provides AI guidance on how to tap into those insights and now lets marketers generate video concepts from static assets, edit hooks, audio, length, overlays, and end scenes. Meta has expanded its Meta Ads MCP server to support more use cases, allowing advertisers to integrate third‑party AI tools for campaign building and management. Customer Lifecycle Strategy is now available to all advertisers, enabling them to set a top‑level audience focus that guides all campaign recommendations. New AI‑powered video tools let users create video from catalog listings and add related‑product recommendations for upselling. Meta is working with Shopify to enable direct purchases of Shopify products inside Messenger via the Meta Business Agent. Similar AI‑driven checkout tests are underway for Meta AI with Adyen, PayPa
Source: Marketing Dive (https://marketingdive.com/news/meta-introduces-new-ai-powered-tools-at-advertising-week/832517)

item.title: Next, Primark and Tesco fund WRAP’s overhaul of UK textile collection
item.description:
Next, Primark and Tesco funded the initial phase of WRAP’s Textiles Collections Transition Program after the nonprofit published its first report on Thursday. WRAP will hold stakeholder workshops from October through January to develop a Blueprint slated for publication in spring 2027. The charity said prices for used textiles collected through charity shops fell more than 80 percent between January 2024 and January 2026.
U.K. textile collectors and sorters faced an “88-million-pounds-a-year loss”—about $116 million—according to WRAP’s May 2025 assessment. In 2021, household recycling centers discarded around 711,000 metric tons of used textiles, representing 49 percent of the UK’s used‑textile flow. Collection trials under the ACT UK project showed that giving citizens more donation opportunities increased volumes by up to 46 percent, though participants struggled to distinguish reusable from non‑reusable items. Asda’s trial letting customers hand over unwanted textiles with grocery deliveries attracted interest but was halted due to waste‑permit requirements.
“Transforming textile collections is an industry-wide challenge that no organization can solve alone,” Catherine David, WRAP’s chief executive officer said.
The initiative follows years of warnings about financial pressures facing the UK’s textile reuse and recycling sector. WRAP’s 2024 Textiles Market Situation Report estimated that household recycling centers discarded around 711,000 metric tons of used textiles in 2021, representing 49 percent of used textiles in the UK.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/wrap-next-primark-tesco-textile-collections-1239333409)

item.title: Shopify adds automated policy generation to speed store launches
item.description:
On October 8, 2026, Shopify introduced automated generation for return and refund, contact information, terms of service, shipping, and legal notice policies to help merchants launch stores faster. The automated policies stay in sync with store settings and Shopify’s recommendations, while merchants remain responsible for ensuring compliance.
Merchants activate the feature by opening Settings > Policies in the Shopify admin interface. They then choose the specific policy they wish to automate from the list of available options. After selecting a policy, they toggle the Use automated policy switch to the on position. Finally, they click the Save button to apply the automation. Once enabled, the system automatically updates the policy whenever the underlying store settings change. This synchronization ensures that the policy reflects the current configuration without manual intervention. The automation applies to five distinct policy types: return and refund, contact information, terms of service, shipping, and legal notice. For each of these policy types, the generated text aligns with Shopify’s current recommendations. Shopify clarifies that the automation does not relieve the store owner of responsibility for the policy’s content. Merchants must still review the automated policies to confirm they meet applicable legal requirements. The feature is intended to reduce the time required to set up a new store or expand into additional markets. By keeping policies up to date automatically, merchants can avoid the need for frequent manual edits as their store evolves.
Source: Shopify Changelog (https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/automatically-generated-policies-help-you-launch-faster)

item.title: Consumers anticipate higher spending as inflation worries climb
item.description:
According to the Fed survey, median expected household spending growth rose to 5.5% in September, the highest since May 2023. Inflation expectations climbed to 3.9%, while the perceived chance of job loss dropped to 13.5%, its lowest since December 2024.
Expected household income growth edged up to 3.1%, its highest since February 2025, while the perceived probability of losing a job fell to 13.5% and the chance of finding new work after a layoff rose to 46.1%. Median year-ahead inflation expectations climbed to 3.9% (highest since May 2023), three-year expectations rose to 3.3%, the five-year measure held at 3.0%, and expected price growth reached 5.5% for food, 4.8% for gas, 6.8% for rent, 7.5% for college and 9.2% for medical care. The Consumer Expectations Index fell 0.7 points to 54.1, the macroeconomic and buying climate subindex slipped 2.2 points to 45.0, buying conditions dropped 1.8 points and personal financial resilience remained near 58.3. Job mobility fell 2.2 points to 46.9, below the neutral level of 50, personal job security remained high at 80.4, perceived safety from layoffs improved to 71.9, and 51.8% of consumers said their savings would cover three months or less if income stopped.
In August, the Consumer Expectations Index had already slipped, marking the second straight month of decline. Personal financial resilience stayed near 58.3 while buying conditions fell 1.8 points. Personal job security stayed at 80.4 and perceived safety from layoffs improved to 71.9.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/economy/2026/consumers-expect-to-spend-more-as-inflation-anxiety-rises)

item.title: SONAR Rate Intelligence adds intermodal rates with 21.1% savings estimate
item.description:
In October 2026, SONAR Rate Intelligence added intermodal contract and spot rates plus a conversion savings tool that shows truckload-to-intermodal savings averaging 21.1% per load. On the Chicago-to-Elizabeth, New Jersey lane, the tool estimates a saving of roughly $593 per load when shifting from van to intermodal.
Users can select intermodal as an equipment type or drill into it from any van lane to view contract and spot rates, resolved ramps, and rate trends. The conversion savings feature calculates estimated savings per load, total lane savings, intermodal volume, and conversion potential, allowing users to input their own rates and annual volume. Data includes intermodal contract rates, spot rates on covered corridors, rate and volume trends over the last 12 months, and suggested in‑gate and out‑gate ramps with distances from origin and destination.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/sonar-rate-intelligence-adds-intermodal-rates-and-truckload-to-intermodal-conversion-savings)

item.title: AI-driven trade surge lifts semiconductors to 42% of global goods growth in 2025
item.description:
Semiconductors, data transmission equipment and data center hardware made up 42% of all goods trade growth in 2025, according to a NYU Stern report commissioned by DHL. That share climbed to roughly 76% in the first quarter of the same year.
FedEx’s chief commercial officer said the addressable transportation market for data centers and IT service equipment is conservatively valued at $7 billion. DHL Global Forwarding estimates the data center logistics market was about $23 billion in 2025 and projects it to reach at least $35 billion by 2030. Analysts estimate cloud providers could spend as much as $525 billion on data center construction in 2026 alone. AI-related supply chains require speed, visibility, cross-border expertise and resilience. This shift demands logistics providers with expertise in handling sensitive, high‑value cargo and navigating complex international regulations.
“The biggest story in global trade right now is AI – not tariffs,” John Pearson, CEO of DHL Express said.
AI infrastructure differs from typical consumer goods because it involves moving large, valuable, and delicate items from Asian factories to worldwide data centers, requiring special handling, customs clearance and storage. U.S. AI investment has boosted imports of related goods even as overall imports of other products have fallen.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/ai-gold-rush-transforms-trans-pacific-trade-and-logistics)

item.title: CBP begins paying IEEPA tariff refunds for finally liquidated entries
item.description:
U.S. Customs and Border Protection has started processing refunds for finally liquidated entries linked to the now‑defunct IEEPA tariffs after an Oct. 6 court filing confirmed eligibility. Only plaintiffs who submitted a valid importer of record number to CBP by July 30, 2026 can currently receive the refunds, while later filers must wait for further guidance.
As of Oct. 6, CBP had accepted 477 CAPE declarations covering 425,517 entries for processing. The agency said importers can apply for the refunds through the Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries (CAPE) portal. The CAPE system is designed to handle roughly $11.4 billion, or 6.9% of the duties imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act that were later struck down by the Supreme Court. As of Oct. 2, CAPE had accepted about $136.6 billion in potential and certified refunds, with $126 billion already forwarded to the Treasury for disbursement. The Court of International Trade earlier this year ruled that CBP must refund unprocessed or unfinalized entries and later expanded the order to include finally liquidated entries, though the Justice Department appealed the decision.
“Organizations can apply for the refunds through CBP's Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries portal, or CAPE,” Brandon Lord, executive director of CBP’s Trade Programs Directorate said.
“Another important step in the CAPE process — and one importers involved in the tariff litigation will want to continue to monitor,” Kelly Nelson, principal consultant and managing director of KPMG Trade & Customs Services said.
The CAPE rollout began earlier this year to process refunds for IEEPA‑related duties after the Supreme Court invalidated them in February. CBP had aimed to launch the third phase for finally liquidated entries by end‑July but postponed it to October, and the Court of International Trade had ordered refunds for unprocessed entries before expanding the order to finally liquidated entrie
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/cbp-starts-paying-out-ieepa-tariff-refunds-for-finally-liquidated-entries/832411)

item.title: Samsung seeks $186 million from CMA CGM over container charges
item.description:
Samsung Electronics America is seeking at least $186 million from CMA CGM in a Federal Maritime Commission complaint that alleges the carrier imposed unlawful container charges and failed to meet inland transportation commitments. The dispute covers store-door shipments that began in January 2020 and includes more than 121,000 demurrage and detention charges Samsung says it paid. Samsung is asking for about $148 million in disputed demurrage, detention, rail storage and related costs.
One example cited in the complaint involves a container shipped from Busan to Long Beach then to The Colony, Texas, which accrued roughly $162,800 in rail storage charges after its service was switched from store-door to container-yard.
CMA CGM has said the dispute stems from the exceptional operating conditions of the Covid-19 pandemic and that it fulfilled its contractual obligations and regulatory requirements. The carrier began handling Samsung’s containers under store-door bills of lading in January 2020, according to the complaint.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/samsung-seeks-186m-from-cma-cgm-in-container-charges-dispute)

item.title: Omaha Steaks launches No Bull campaign to attract Gen Z shoppers
item.description:
Omaha Steaks, which has been around for 109 years, launched its No Bull campaign in September to attract Gen Z shoppers. Roughly two weeks after the launch, conversion rates climbed 46% and social media mentions surged 130%, according to company data.
The No Bull campaign runs across TV, radio, YouTube, podcasts, paid social, and influencer partnerships, building on the earlier ‘America’s Table’ effort that debuted in June with a Kevin Costner‑narrated national ad. Senior Director of Growth Marketing Angie Kubicek said the brand now ties its ‘quality’ claim to U.S. sourcing, extended aging, and hand‑cut by butchers, responding to customer concerns about meat origin. The campaign also addresses a broader industry context, noting that the Trump administration announced plans in September to import about 660 million pounds of lean beef trimmings over 90 days via reduced tariffs.
“Now we're making sure that when we say quality, it stands for something,” Angie Kubicek, Senior Director of Growth Marketing said.
“The brand learned through internal insights that a large number of its customers have expressed that where their meat comes from matters to them,” Angie Kubicek, Senior Director of Growth Marketing said.
Before the No Bull push, Omaha Steaks relied on savings‑driven promotions and vague descriptors like “gourmet” or “quality” to sell its meat. In June the brand debuted the “America’s Table” campaign, which included its first national ad narrated by Kevin Costner and highlighted the dinner table’s role in historic moments.
Source: Marketing Dive (https://marketingdive.com/news/inside-omaha-steaks-efforts-to-ditch-marketing-bull-and-attract-gen-z/832062)

item.title: Rust Coast Deploys Real-Time Computer Vision to Cut Apparel Fit Errors
item.description:
Rust Coast founder Kyle Valade has introduced a turnkey computer vision system that uses factory‑floor cameras to automatically measure garments and compare them to specifications in real time. The system sends images to an app where analytics are generated and alerts are pushed to the brand’s portal, aiming to capture a picture of each item throughout production.
Cameras are installed across factories and take pictures passively without interfering with workers. Visual AI processes the images to automatically measure the clothing made by suppliers. The system compares those measurements with the product’s specification in real time. Photos and data are sent to Rust Coast’s app for more intensive processing that generates analytics and alerts. Those alerts are then pushed to the brand’s portal for review. The company is working toward capturing a picture of each piece of clothing throughout the entire manufacturing process. Valade says the technology will save companies millions by ensuring correctly sized products are always shipped. Before founding Rust Coast, Valade worked at Rivian for several years, helping to pull in and organize petabytes of vehicle data. He initially launched Rust Coast to digitize manual, pencil‑and‑paper processes in factories, starting with garment measurements. Many factory processes remain pencil‑and‑paper even when machines are advanced and digital. He began by examining the beanies production line, noting that each step—yarn knitting, fabric cutting, folding, sewing, labeling, and final measurement—must be correct or the whole item is ruined.
“that will save companies millions by ensuring correctly sized products are always shipped,” Kyle Valade, founder of Rust Coast Manufacturing Technology said.
