item.title: Revlon reports 9.8‑times higher CTR from Amazon interactive video ads
item.description:
In June, Revlon used Amazon’s Interactive Video Ads and Dynamic TV Creative to achieve a 9.8‑times higher click‑through rate versus non‑interactive ads. The same campaign also lifted branded search rates by two times and return on ad spend by 2.6 times versus category benchmarks.
Interactive Video Ads retain the brand’s original 15‑ or 30‑second creative while adding an overlay that lets viewers take action without leaving the streaming experience. Amazon’s Dynamic TV Creative automatically personalizes the ad’s format, call‑to‑action, headline and other elements based on real‑time shopping signals, using a one‑click activation after the advertiser uploads the asset. The technology draws on Amazon’s trove of consumer data to match creative to where shoppers are in their purchase journey, optimizing for interactivity. Revlon’s chief digital marketing officer said the ease of use is critical, noting that the harder the process, the less likely the brand is to adopt it. The findings were shared during an Advertising Week New York panel on Oct. 7, where Revlon and Amazon executives discussed the campaign’s impact on full‑funnel marketing.
“We love a good 15-second [ad],” Kelly Solomon, chief digital marketing officer at Revlon said.
Amazon introduced Dynamic TV Creative at its May upfront presentation, combining trillions of consumer data points and AI to personalize interactive video ads.
Source: Marketing Dive (https://marketingdive.com/news/how-revlon-used-amazons-interactive-video-ads-to-drive-outcomes/832462)

item.title: Shipt names Raj Kapoor as CEO effective Oct. 18
item.description:
Shipt appointed Raj Kapoor as its next chief executive officer, with the change taking effect on October 18. Kapoor previously served as Shipt’s chief operating officer from 2022 to 2025 before moving to Target, and he succeeds Kamau Witherspoon, who had led the company for over four years.
During his three-year run as COO, Kapoor scaled Shipt’s fulfillment engine, improved quality and service, and led day-to-day operations. At Target, he drove profitable growth, expanded assortment and improved the customer experience on Target Plus. Shipt remains a wholly owned Target subsidiary, acquired in 2017. The leadership shift coincides with Shipt’s recent AI push, including the September launch of Ask Shipt, an AI-powered shopping assistant that can build carts from conversation or photos and suggest budget‑friendly meals.
“I’m excited to rejoin Shipt, work with Target and our partners, and lead a team whose care and dedication I know firsthand. My focus is simple: enhance convenience for our customers, empower our shopper and driver community, and strengthen business performance across our offerings,” Raj Kapoor, incoming CEO said.
Kamau Witherspoon had led Shipt for four-plus years and will remain through late October to support the transition. Witherspoon spent more than 15 years at Target, and during his tenure he integrated the Shipt marketplace as a benefit for Target Circle 360 members. Shipt was acquired by Target in 2017.
Source: Grocery Dive (https://grocerydive.com/news/shipt-names-ceo-raj-kapoor-target/832478)

item.title: Survey shows 81% of finance leaders faced AI‑linked fraud attempts in past year
item.description:
Early Warning Services’ Certos unit surveyed 230 senior financial leaders between August 7 and 21, finding that 81% reported an attempted fraud involving AI‑generated content in the last year. Seventy‑nine percent said they were concerned that such fraud could damage trust in their organization, while 43% pointed to payment diversion as their top worry.
Eighty‑four percent of respondents said AI‑enabled fraud is much or somewhat harder to detect than traditional schemes. Only half felt confident they could spot such fraud before money left the company, despite 87% believing they were somewhat prepared. Ninety‑three percent said the risk is changing how they view their financial‑institution partners, and 51% want those partners to provide better detection of suspicious activity.
“Biggest concern is a convincing fake request slipping through and sending company money to the wrong place,” anonymous CFO of a Fortune 500 company said.
“AI can make fraud easier to create, scale and disguise,” Certos spokesperson said.
Certos’ report comes at a time when businesses across many industries continue to loudly and enthusiastically embrace new AI tools in the name of productivity, even as purveyors of the technology themselves continue to issue dire warnings about the threats posed by their own products.
Source: Payments Dive (https://paymentsdive.com/news/finance-leaders-fight-deepfakes-Certos-fraud-prevention/832475)

item.title: ThredUp CEO says AI costs surprised him but won't curb usage
item.description:
At the RetailClub AI Festival in California last month, ThredUp CEO James Reinhart said AI implementation costs surprised him but will not slow employee use, even as the company reported Q2 revenue up about 17% to $90.8 million. ThredUp's Q2 operating expenses rose more than 17% to roughly $78.6 million while net loss grew 15% to $5.9 million.
Reinhart noted that the company's token usage has increased faster than he originally anticipated. He argued that slowing employee AI use would be a mistake because the technology will eventually deliver significant cost savings by limiting headcount growth and raising team productivity. To illustrate his commitment, Reinhart showed a slide deck he had never seen before that was generated by Claude and reviewed by his own assistant, calling the exercise an interesting experiment.
“I was both surprised and didn't care at all,” James Reinhart, co-founder and CEO of ThredUp said.
“I'm confident that advancements in AI technology will provide significant cost savings for the business by reducing the need to grow headcount as fast and by helping our teams to be more productive,” James Reinhart, co-founder and CEO of ThredUp said.
The costs of implementing AI across enterprises has surprised some executives in recent months, but ThredUp is pursuing an AI-first strategy. As a public company, Reinhart said at the RetailClub AI Festival that ThredUp just needs to get better at projecting these costs.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/thredup-ceo-ai-costs/831921)

item.title: DailyObjects raises ₹332 Cr in Series C to expand offline retail
item.description:
DailyObjects has raised ₹332 Cr ($34.3 Mn) in a Series C funding round co-led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital. The round valued the startup at ₹1,050 Cr ($108.4 Mn) and included both primary and secondary transactions.
The fresh capital of ₹332 Cr ($34.3 Mn) raised in the Series C round will be deployed to scale DailyObjects' offline network across India. Part of the funds will deepen the company's product and R&D capabilities, focusing on its core lifestyle and tech accessories such as phone cases, watchbands, bags, wallets and wireless chargers. Additionally, the proceeds will strengthen brand building efforts and help evaluate opportunities in international markets. As part of the offline expansion strategy, DailyObjects aims to open 150 exclusive brand outlets (EBOs) across India over the next five years. The Series C round, which included both primary and secondary transactions, valued the startup at ₹1,050 Cr ($108.4 Mn) and was co-led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital. In the secondary component of the round, early investor Roots Ventures partially exited, realizing an 18X return on its initial $2 Mn investment made in February 2022, having previously doubled down during the company's $10 Mn Series B funding round in 2024.
Roots Ventures first invested $2 Mn in DailyObjects in February 2022. Following which, the investor doubled down on the startup during its $10 Mn Series B funding round in 2024.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/d2c-lifestyle-brand-dailyobjects-raises-%E2%82%B9332-cr-to-expand-offline-presence)

item.title: FTC orders Gildan and S&S to end T-shirt pricing restrictions
item.description:
The Federal Trade Commission announced that it has secured changes to the partnership agreement between Gildan Activewear SRL and wholesale distributor S&S Holdings LLC to remove pricing restrictions that favored S&S over competitors. The revised agreement states that nothing in it restricts Gildan’s discretion to set prices or offer partnership support to any other North American wholesale distributor.
The FTC investigated Gildan for potential violations of Section 2(a) of the Robinson-Patman Act, which prohibits sellers from engaging in certain price discrimination. After the amendment, the FTC closed its investigation and posted a public letter from Gildan confirming the contract change. The action follows an RPA settlement with Southern Glazer’s Wine and Spirits, the largest U.S. wine and spirits distributor, which was the first federal enforcement case in over 20 years.
“Congress has prohibited unfair and discriminatory pricing practices that favor big businesses and box out small businesses, which are the engine of the American economy,” Daniel Guarnera said.
Last week the FTC entered an RPA settlement with Southern Glazer’s Wine and Spirits, the largest U.S. distributor of wine and spirits. That settlement was the first RPA case resolved by a federal enforcement agency in over 20 years.
Source: FTC Press Releases (https://ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/10/ftc-secures-fair-pricing-protections-taking-action-against-major-wholesale-t-shirt-distributors)

item.title: Zalando opens 140,000‑square‑metre new distribution centre in France
item.description:
Zalando has officially opened its first mega‑distribution centre in France, a 140,000‑square‑metre facility in Montereau-sur-le-Jard just south of Paris, after five years of planning and construction. The centre fulfills the 300‑million‑euro investment pledge made by founder and CEO Robert Gentz at the 2021 Choose France summit.
The site will ramp up gradually to full capacity, eventually processing a significant portion of Zalando’s French online orders, reflecting the company’s gradual growth strategy. Positioned on the outskirts of Paris, the complex is intended to speed up deliveries across western Europe, strengthen the company’s logistics network, and support its European expansion. Zalando describes the facility as one of the most beautiful and modern locations in its entire European network, according to its Managing Director for Western Europe. The opening marks the German e‑commerce giant’s first mega‑distribution centre in France, extending its footprint beyond Germany and neighbouring markets and underscoring its commitment to the French market.
“Back then, it was just a promise. Today, this investment is taking shape in a 140,000 m² facility—one of the most beautiful and modern locations in our entire European network,” Laura Toledano Khelif, Zalando’s Managing Director for Western Europe said.
Planning for the centre began five years before its opening, with the early work starting before the launch. In 2021, Robert Gentz announced the 300‑million‑euro investment at the Choose France summit, framing it as a long‑term commitment to the French market. The facility’s location in Montereau-sur-le-Jard was chosen for its proximity to the major transport corridors serving Paris and surrounding regions.
Source: RetailDetail EU (https://retaildetail.eu/news/fashion/zalando-sets-up-shop-in-france-with-a-giant-distribution-center)

item.title: Asendia’s e-PAQ GO gives retailers access to over 250,000 European OOH points
item.description:
Asendia’s e-PAQ GO now gives retailers access to over 250,000 out-of-home lockers and collection points across key European markets. The service comes as 72% of global retailers say they remain optimistic about international growth despite tariffs and trade tensions.
e-PAQ GO is described as plug‑and‑play global logistics that removes the need for retailers to manage multiple carrier contracts. The platform is API‑ready, so it can be connected to existing e‑commerce systems without custom development. By consolidating customs declarations, tax calculations, and tracking numbers, it aims to minimise clearance delays at borders. Retailers can present shoppers with the three most common OOH options in Europe – lockers, parcel shops, and home delivery – through a single checkout integration. In Poland, lockers are the preferred pickup point; in France, parcel shops dominate; in the United Kingdom, most consumers still expect doorstep service. Offering the locally familiar choice is intended to increase post‑purchase satisfaction and encourage repeat purchases from international buyers. Asendia says the offering reduces the overhead normally associated with setting up separate international delivery networks. By providing a consistent returns process through the same OOH points, it also helps close the loop on cross‑border orders. The company cites the Asendia Global 360 Report to show that optimism about overseas expansion remains high even amid trade uncertainty. Ultimately, the goal is to convert the logistical simplicity of OOH delivery into stronger brand loyalty across borders.
Source: InternetRetailing (https://internetretailing.net/why-out-of-home-delivery-unlocks-global-reach)

item.title: Connecticut man sentenced to two years for $3.5M Amazon trucking fraud
item.description:
Ameer Nasir, a 25‑year‑old from Trumbull, Connecticut, was sentenced on Wednesday to two years in federal prison for defrauding Amazon Logistics of more than $3.5 million. He had registered 23 trucking accounts with Amazon Relay, which prosecutors tied to over 1,000 nonexistent trailer moves.
The scheme ran from December 2019 through February 2021, during which Nasir used the accounts to obtain transportation assignments and falsely check trailers in and out via Amazon Relay. Prosecutors said he evaded Relay’s GPS geofencing safeguard by misusing the platform’s manual override, and one May 16, 2020, assignment from Kent, Washington, to Lakeland, Florida, was billed at $4,566.41 although the trailer never moved. Nasir pleaded guilty to one wire fraud count on March 6, 2026, and the court ordered $3,547,090.93 in restitution plus three years of supervised release.
Amazon has since added identity and driver verification measures to its Relay platform to curb fraud, according to earlier FreightWaves reporting. The scheme ended in February 2021, and the indictment shows Nasir exploited the system more than five years ago, leaving uncertain whether a similar fraud could succeed today.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/man-gets-2-years-for-3-5m-amazon-fraud-using-23-trucking-accounts)

item.title: Australian shoppers plan to spend $346 on Black Friday, up from $324 last year
item.description:
Australian shoppers intend to spend an average of $346 over the 2026 Black Friday Cyber Monday period, up from $324 last year, according to Shopify’s holiday retail report. This rise contrasts with a global decline in planned spending from $276 to $268, while 54% of respondents said economic conditions influenced their holiday purchases, prompting extra research before buying.
The report found that 85% of Australian shoppers prefer waiting to purchase a specific item rather than choosing an immediate alternative, compared with a global average of 79%. It also showed that 62% of Australian consumers expect to use AI tools for deal discovery and product comparison, with 70% of shoppers aged 25 to 34 already using such tools versus 45% across all age groups. Among businesses, 51% are investing in AI-generated content, 46% in virtual assistants and 45% in optimising store platforms for AI recommendation engines. The findings also highlight shifting merchant choices, with 54% of respondents reporting increased purchases from independent or niche brands compared to the previous year.
“Australians are still willing to spend this holiday season, but they’re putting more work into deciding what’s worth their money,” James Johnson, head of enterprise ANZ at Shopify said.
The findings come from Shopify’s holiday retail report. Australian consumers anticipate higher spending during the 2026 Black Friday Cyber Monday period even amid ongoing economic pressures.
Source: Internet Retailing Australia (https://internetretailing.com.au/australian-shoppers-set-to-increase-black-friday-spending)

item.title: Fast Retailing posts 32% profit rise to 743.1 billion yen
item.description:
Fast Retailing reported operating profit of 743.13 billion yen for the year ended August 31, a rise of about 32 percent from 564.3 billion yen a year earlier. The company forecast operating profit of 830 billion yen for the year ending August 2027, exceeding its own 730 billion yen target and the average analyst estimate of 726.45 billion yen.
Fast Retailing operates more than 2,500 Uniqlo stores worldwide, with nearly 900 of them in China, its largest foreign market. A weak yen raised import costs in Japan, pressuring fourth‑quarter results and prompting the company to consider price increases there. Fast Retailing plans to double the number of its flagship‑store format in Japan to 20 over the next decade to counter online competition and revive foot traffic.
The Uniqlo operator has beaten quarterly expectations throughout the year and repeatedly raised its profit guidance. Fast Retailing traces its origins to a single Uniqlo store opened in Hiroshima in 1984 and has since expanded to over 2,500 stores worldwide.
Source: Inside Retail Asia (https://insideretail.asia/2026/10/08/uniqlo-parent-fast-retailing-shocks-with-32-per-cent-profit-boost)

item.title: WEX executive says AI agents need payment controls to act safely
item.description:
At the PYMNTS B2B Payments Event 2026, Ryan Taylor, SVP Product Management – Mobility & Payments at WEX, said AI agents need three elements—context, controls, and clarity—to act safely. He noted that virtual cards already restrict merchant, amount, timing and transaction count, turning those limits into programmable permissions for machines.
Payment data supplies the context AI needs, showing who is spending, where money moves, what is bought and whether a transaction looks odd. While AI can decide that an invoice should be paid or a fuel purchase is legitimate, only the payment system can enforce whether the agent actually has authority to move the money. Taylor warned against giving agents open-ended access to corporate bank accounts, saying controls must govern how and when they can execute payments and how money flows to manage risk. He suggested the future enterprise payments stack could work less like traditional plumbing and more like an API that grants financial authority on demand.
“Taylor argued that effective artificial intelligence systems therefore require three elements: context, controls and clarity,” Ryan Taylor, SVP Product Management – Mobility & Payments at WEX said.
“One of the main reasons virtual cards are so compelling as we look towards an agentic future is that controls are built directly into the payments themselves,” Ryan Taylor, SVP Product Management – Mobility & Payments at WEX said.
Before this discussion, enterprises had to stitch together operational data and payment execution manually, a process that created delays and errors as transaction volumes grew. AI systems have improved at spotting suspicious invoices, fueling anomalies and price drifts, but they lacked the authority to act on those insights.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/b2b-payments/2026/b2b-payments-already-have-the-controls-ai-agents-need)

item.title: PYMNTS report splits U.S. consumers into three spending groups as prices rise
item.description:
PYMNTS Intelligence’s 2026 analysis finds that 45% of U.S. adults keep spending flat or raise it despite higher bills, while 34% cut both spending and savings and 21% boost income or rely on installment plans. Among the proactive group, 48% use buy now, pay later to manage expenses, compared with just 8% of the reactive group.
The report also notes that 66% of all consumers have reduced everyday spending and 51% have avoided large purchases, yet only 21% have tried negotiating bills. Side work is common, with 37.6% of workers having taken on extra jobs in the prior six months to supplement income. Within the baby‑boomer generation, 69% of reactive consumers report daily living pressure, a 31‑point gap versus the 38% of balanced boomers facing the same strain.
PYMNTS Intelligence’s “The Fragmented Paycheck: Why Rising Spending No Longer Means Stronger Demand,” part of The American Paycheck 2026 Annual Edition, examines how households earn, spend and manage financial pressure. It draws on four research programs covering financial lifestyles, generational behavior, credit use and consumer expectations.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/consumer-insights/2026/higher-prices-are-splitting-consumers-into-three-camps)

item.title: Amazon cuts about 1,000 roles in latest workforce reduction
item.description:
Amazon eliminated approximately 1,000 roles across its Stores, customer service, marketplace support and retail engineering teams on 6 October 2026. The cuts were disclosed via internal emails and affected employees in India and the UK, according to messages from an internal Slack channel with nearly 37,000 members. These reductions follow two earlier rounds that removed about 30,000 roles in October 2025 and January 2026.
An Amazon spokesperson told Business Insider that only a small number of positions, mainly in the Stores business, were eliminated that day. Employees asked about severance packages, medical leave, internal transfer options and whether further notifications would follow. Amazon has also reached out to former workers, including those from prior layoffs, to fill openings in its Amazon Web Services and artificial intelligence divisions.
“a small number,” Amazon spokesperson said.
Since late 2022, Amazon has eliminated more than 57,000 corporate positions. This includes the 16,000 roles cut in January 2026 and the roughly 30,000 roles removed in the two rounds announced in October 2025 and January 2026.
Source: Retail Insight Network (https://retail-insight-network.com/news/amazon-cuts-approximately-1000-roles)

item.title: RBI clarifies FEMA rules, exempts personal transactions and tutoring payments
item.description:
RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra yesterday clarified that individuals undertaking personal‑nature transactions, overseas tutoring payments, and small software assignments are exempt from reporting under the new FEMA rules that took effect on October 1. The framework lets exporters file a self‑declaration for each export bill up to ₹10 lakh, with banks handling the reporting to the RBI.
Banks and authorised dealers will now receive the export declarations and match them with remittances, replacing the earlier SOFTEX process for software exports and the separate goods‑export declaration. The regulations introduce a single Export Declaration Form (EDF) that can cover a month’s worth of service exports, including software, allowing exporters to file one form instead of multiple. For each bill not exceeding ₹10 lakh, exporters may submit a self‑declaration to their authorised dealer, which the bank can then close in the export‑monitoring system once payment is realised. Exporters also have the option to file these self‑declarations quarterly, enabling bulk closure of eligible entries in the export‑monitoring system. The RBI said it will publish FAQs to help freelancers, creators and SaaS founders understand how the clarification applies to their specific arrangements, especially regarding overseas tutoring and small software assignments.
“From a founder's perspective, there's not a whole lot of change... what was being filed in SOFTEX, they'll go by and file it in EDF and the banks have to match,” Naganand Doraswamy, founder and managing partner at Ideaspring Capital said.
“consolidating export reporting through authorised banks could simplify compliance for software and AI startups,” Manav Garg, cofounder and managing partner at Together Fund said.
Before the change, software exporters used the SOFTEX platform for reporting, while goods exports followed a separate declaration process. Other service exports did not necessarily require equivalent declarations, although ex
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/new-fema-rules-explained-what-freelancers-creators-and-saas-startups-need-to-know)

item.title: UPI MDR rollout may be pushed to January 2027 amid retailer pushback
item.description:
The National Payments Corporation of India‑led UPI and Services Steering Committee is weighing a deferral of the merchant discount rate on select UPI transactions from October 15 to January 1, 2027, following opposition from retail trader groups. Under the proposed framework, a 0.40% fee would apply to person‑to‑merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 per transaction, while businesses with up to ₹40 lakh annual turnover could be exempted and payments below the threshold would remain free of charge.
For bill payments, utilities, education and fuel, the fee would be a flat ₹5 on each transaction exceeding ₹2,000. Consumers would not bear the MDR, and the acquiring bank would retain 0.28% of the transaction value as interchange, passing 0.12% to the issuing bank and 0.08% to the UPI app provider. Authorities are also reviewing a raise in the daily UPI transaction limit for certain sectors from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh. In September, UPI processed 24.07 billion transactions worth ₹29.37 trillion, with volume up 22.6% year‑on‑year and value up 18% year‑on‑year. The fee would create a new revenue stream for banks, payment service providers and third‑party application providers.
The MDR would end the current zero‑fee regime for most merchant UPI payments, a shift that the Centre said would leave about 96% of transactions unaffected. Retailer associations have opposed the fee, arguing it would raise costs for thin‑margin businesses and had called for a ‘No UPI Day’ on October 2 before withdrawing the protest after a meeting with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on September 30.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/upi-mdr-rollout-may-be-deferred-to-january-2027-amid-pushback-by-retailers)

item.title: Ty Symonds joins Pottery for the Planet as GM effective October 12
item.description:
Pottery for the Planet appointed former Country Road Home GM Ty Symonds as its general manager, effective October 12, bringing more than two decades of retail and design leadership. The brand, founded in 2015 by potter Renton Bishopric, now supplies over 500 wholesale stockists across Australia and New Zealand and operates showrooms in Noosa and Eumundi.
Symonds will relocate from Victoria to work at the company’s fully solar‑powered studio in Noosaville on Queensland’s Sunshine Coast, which also partners with a production facility in Vietnam. Pottery for the Planet makes solar‑fired ceramic travel cups, tableware, and other homewares, selling them through its online store and wholesale network. Before this role, Symonds held senior positions at Kmart Australia, Target Australia, and the fashion label BlackMilk after leading Country Road Home’s creative direction and operations.
“Bringing Ty on is a sign of where we’re heading,” Renton Bishopric, founder of Pottery for the Planet said.
“Australian consumers are asking harder questions about where things are made and what they are made of, and the brands answering those questions properly are the ones growing,” Ty Symonds, GM of Pottery for the Planet said.
Founded in 2015, Pottery for the Planet started with solar‑fired ceramic travel cups as an alternative to single‑use plastic and has since expanded its ceramic range.
Source: Inside Retail Australia (https://insideretail.com.au/careers/appointments-exits/ex-country-road-gm-ty-symonds-to-lead-pottery-for-the-planet-202610)

item.title: Panda teams with Spike, GoWit to boost Saudi e‑commerce media
item.description:
Panda Retail, with more than 200 stores, teams with Spike Media Saudi and GoWit to boost its e‑commerce media operations ahead of the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November. The partnership will give Panda access to over 14 million online shoppers and one million monthly active app visits, expanding advertiser participation and enabling more automated, data‑driven media operations.
GoWit will supply the technology infrastructure, including first party data activation, AI powered auction and bidding, campaign automation, and real time measurement and reporting. Spike Media Saudi, operating locally as GoSpike, contributes local market expertise and advertiser relationships. Panda says the collaboration will help scale its retail media business across physical and digital channels. The initiative aims to create greater opportunities for brands to connect with shoppers across the Kingdom.
“As we continue our digital transformation, e-commerce media gives us new opportunities to connect brands with our customers in relevant and measurable ways,” Ahmad Chehade, CMO at Panda Retail said.
“We are proud to work alongside Panda as a success partner for its e-commerce media journey,” Osama Bukhari, CEO at Spike Media Saudi said.
Retail media will be a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards. The awards, which celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world, have now closed for entries. Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/7/grocery-retailer-panda-teams-with-spike-and-gowit-to-power-e-commerce-media-push-in-saudi-arabia)

item.title: OK Future creates Goodwipes AI spoof in four days, cutting projected $700k cost
item.description:
OK Future produced Goodwipes’ 'Meet Asstra' social media spot, a spoof of OpenAI’s Astra commercial, using generative AI tools in just four days. In its first 48 hours on Reddit, the spot garnered more than 750,000 views, later climbing to nearly 1.5 million across subreddits and accumulating over 800 shares according to a company spokesperson.
Typically a minute‑long commercial takes about six weeks, but OK Future compressed the workflow into four days by using AI for character visualization, voice‑over and location generation. The four‑person team worked in shifts around the clock on little sleep, with one member threatening to quit at 2 a.m. before returning at 7 a.m. after tensions eased. Cartagena said AI struggled with editing text and the team questioned whether the spot would finish on time and be well‑received. Goodwipes has not calculated exact savings, but its SVP of marketing said the AI‑produced spot cost less than a traditional location scout, production team, director and post‑production edit.
“It was sort of like a pressure cooker because you take what is normally the emotions of a month and a half shoot, and compress them into four days,” Frank Cartagena, founder of OK Future said.
“It’s not just about speed. It’s about trust, and I have a lot of trust in Frank,” Meredith Diehn, SVP of marketing at Goodwipes said.
OK Future was launched earlier this year by Frank Cartagena after his tenure as CEO of MullenLowe U.S., aiming to test how generative AI could let a small agency punch above its weight. Goodwipes had begun experimenting with AI‑powered creative, relying on OK Future and its internal team for guidance while navigating legal approvals and internal stakeholder comfort.
Source: Digiday (https://digiday.com/marketing/inside-agency-ok-futures-ai-pressure-cooker-experiment-with-goodwipes)

item.title: Three fashion brands surpass $100 million revenue without outside investment
item.description:
Three fashion brands, including Aviator Nation and SwissWatchExpo, have each surpassed $100 million in annual revenue without taking any outside investment. Their growth arrives as U.S. venture capital dropped to a six‑year low of $66 billion in 2025, a decline of 35% from the previous year.
Aviator Nation began in 2006 when founder Paige Mycoskie hand‑stitched clothes and sold them at Los Angeles street fairs, later taking only an $8,000 Wells Fargo bank loan to start operations. Mycoskie said she bootstrapped everything, kept costs low by doing her own photography, website programming and sewing, and she manages inventory with weekly sales reports to avoid over‑ or under‑stocking. SwissWatchExpo, founded by Jake and Victoria Rokhlin and now led by CEO Eugene Tutunikov, operates mainly online with one Atlanta store and holds about 2,500 pre‑owned luxury watches, generating over $100 million in annual sales. In September Aviator Nation struck a licensing deal with the NFL to create a collection featuring its 1970s‑inspired designs for 25 teams.
“When I started, I bootstrapped everything and kept operating costs super low because I was able to do most things myself,” Paige Mycoskie, Founder, Aviator Nation said.
“investor expectations can sometimes force leadership to prioritize short-term, headline-grabbing hyper-growth over long-term stability,” Eugene Tutunikov, CEO, SwissWatchExpo said.
During the late 2010s, low interest rates left venture capital eager to invest in fashion startups. More recently, the funding environment has tightened, pushing many brands to rely solely on their own resources.
Source: Glossy (https://glossy.co/fashion/fashion-briefing-how-3-fashion-brands-crossed-100-million-in-revenue-without-outside-investment)

item.title: Tesco appoints Alex Avisse-Williams as Home & Clothing Digital Director
item.description:
Tesco has appointed Alex Avisse-Williams as Digital Director for Home & Clothing, following his departure from Marks & Spencer earlier this year after an almost nine‑year stint. Before joining Tesco, he led online experience and performance marketing at M&S, where he helped shape the retailer’s digital strategy.
He said he intends to build on the momentum of the F&F brand’s online direct‑to‑customer launch over the past 18 months. He also praised Tesco’s fulfilment operation, noting that every order he placed for his family arrived on time. Tesco is trialling AIUTA‑powered virtual try‑on technology at its Sandhurst Extra store, letting customers view around 1,500 F&F items via a digital screen. The virtual try‑on screen allows shoppers to either upload a photo of themselves or select a digital model to see how garments fit in different sizes. The trial forms part of a wider F&F refresh that includes new changing rooms, a dedicated service hub, a larger in‑store range and updated signage and lighting. He said he is excited to join Tesco at a time when the F&F brand is gaining traction online and in‑store.
“I've been making lots of orders in recent weeks for the whole family, and every single one has arrived on time, so well done fulfilment operation,” Alex Avisse-Williams, Digital Director for Home & Clothing at Tesco said.
Avisse‑Williams left Marks & Spencer earlier this year after almost nine years, where he served as Head of Online Experience & Performance Marketing. In a LinkedIn post, he said the F&F team has created excitement around the brand and relaunched F&F online direct to customers over the past 18 months. He noted that the F&F team’s work over the past 18 months has created excitement around the brand and prepared the ground for his arrival.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/7/marks-and-spencer-veteran-alex-avisse-williams-takes-on-digital-director-for-home-clothing-role-at-tesco)

item.title: UK retailers face £440 million rise in electricity costs this year
item.description:
UK retailers are set to see their electricity bills increase by £440 million in 2026, despite unchanged energy use, according to a British Retail Consortium report. The report projects electricity costs to climb from £2.72 billion in 2025 to £3.16 billion in 2026, a 16% rise driven largely by growing non‑commodity charges.
Transmission Network Use of System charges alone are forecast to jump by 72%, adding almost £200 million to retailers’ annual electricity bills. Non‑commodity charges, which include government levies and volatile network costs, now typically make up about two‑thirds of a retailer’s electricity bill. Following decarbonisation investments, roughly 90% of the retail sector’s energy consumption is now electricity, leaving the industry especially exposed to price swings in the power market. Over the past two years, retailers have already absorbed £6.5 billion in extra employment costs, including higher national insurance contributions and living‑wage increases above inflation.
“With another £440 million increase this year despite their energy use barely changing, the Chancellor must take action to reduce the plethora of policy levies, as well as stabilise the predictability of network charges that are driving up the cost of energy,” Helen Dickinson, Chief Executive at the British Retail Consortium said.
The industry has already been hit by £6.5 billion in additional employment costs over the past two years, including higher employer national insurance contributions, above inflationary increases to the national living wage and other employment related costs.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/7/urgent-action-needed-as-uk-retailers-energy-bills-push-up-the-price-of-everyday-essentials-for-shoppers)

item.title: On taps SSI Group to launch first dedicated Philippine stores
item.description:
On is entering the Philippine market with SSI Group as its wholesale and retail distributor in the country. The partnership will open the Philippines’ first dedicated On stores and manage wholesale distribution through On’s third‑party network.
Founded in 2010, On is best known for its patented CloudTec cushioning technology and sells footwear and sportswear through direct‑to‑consumer, wholesale and retail channels worldwide. SSI Group said it will use its expertise in brand development, retail operations, marketing and omnichannel distribution to expand On’s presence in the local Philippine market. SSI Group is one of the Philippines’ largest specialty retail operators, overseeing Rustan’s department store and a portfolio of luxury labels that includes Hermès, Cartier and Salvatore Ferragamo. SSI will open the country’s first dedicated On stores and oversee wholesale distribution through On’s third‑party distribution network.
“We look forward to strengthening the presence of this exceptional brand and are confident it will inspire a new generation of runners, athletes, and active lifestyle enthusiasts,” SSI Group CEO Anthony Huang said.
SSI Group’s profit has sunk as shoppers cut back on luxury spending. On is a Swiss sportswear brand founded in 2010 and best known for its patented CloudTec cushioning technology.
Source: Inside Retail Asia (https://insideretail.asia/2026/10/08/on-taps-ssi-group-to-drive-philippines-expansion)

item.title: Argos expands marketplace to 130,000 products in biggest range push
item.description:
Argos plans to offer more than 130,000 products from vetted third‑party retailers and brands on its Trusted Sellers marketplace by the end of 2026. The platform, which was trialled with 40 partners in July, already offers more than 70,000 products. The expansion marks the biggest increase in Argos’s product range in its history.
Initially focused on furniture, home, and toys, Trusted Sellers is now expanding into health and beauty, gifting and electricals, with beauty brands such as Clarins, Dermalogica, and Medicube already available. Products are delivered directly by Trusted Sellers, although customers can still earn Nectar Points on marketplace purchases. The expansion forms part of a wider transformation programme at Argos that includes investment in its digital experience, rapid delivery, Argos Pay, and other customer propositions. Every partner is vetted by Argos before joining Trusted Sellers, ensuring that products meet the retailer’s quality and safety standards.
“The launch of Trusted Sellers enables us to complement those ranges with thousands of new lines from brands and independent businesses that mean our customers get an even wider range,” Graham Biggart said.
In July, Argos trialled the Trusted Sellers marketplace with 40 partners, offering over 70,000 products. The expansion comes after Sainsbury’s agreed to sell Argos to Swift Partners for £120 million in July, ending ten years of ownership since acquiring the brand for £1.4 billion in 2016. Graham Biggart said the feedback on and from Trusted Sellers has been incredibly positive.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/argos-marketplace-range-push)

item.title: Xeneta says Hormuz freight shock may have peaked after 344% rate surge
item.description:
Xeneta reported that container rates from China to the U.S. East and West Coasts have risen 344 percent and 335 percent since February 28, but the market has likely reached its post‑Hormuz crisis peak. The spread between the two coasts has widened to $3,177 per 40‑foot equivalent unit, with East‑Coast bound containers averaging $11,523 and West‑Coast bound boxes averaging $8,346.
Xeneta forecasts that, looking three months ahead, spot rates could fall to $6,000‑$7,000 for East‑Coast destinations and $4,500‑$5,500 for the West Coast. The UAE’s National Association of Freight and Logistics notes that moving cargo into the Persian Gulf now costs three to five times pre‑war levels due to surcharges, rerouting and land‑transport expenses. Maritime security sources recorded at least 12 attacks on oil, LNG and LPG tankers in the week of September 28 to October 5, the highest weekly total since the conflict began. The International Maritime Organization separately verified nine of those incidents, up from a previous weekly high of eight in mid‑July.
“We can say with a level of confidence that the market has reached its post-Hormuz crisis peak in 2026,” Peter Sand, chief analyst at ocean and air freight benchmarking platform Xeneta said.
“The spread will narrow as the broader decline takes hold in the remainder of the year, driven mainly by a harder fall into the U.S. East Coast due to its more elevated starting point,” Peter Sand, chief analyst at Xeneta said.
Before the Hormuz crisis, the cost gap between East and West Coast shipments was just $772 per 40‑foot unit. In the week of July 13, maritime logs recorded eight vessel attacks, the prior peak.
Source: WWD (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/logistics/strait-of-hormuz-freight-rates-peaked-iran-war-xeneta-container-shipping-oil-1239320306)

item.title: Report urges brands to build farmer ties for better cotton traceability
item.description:
Ani Wells and Anne Oudard released the fourth installment of their five-year #WhoMadeMyCotton investigation on World Cotton Day, arguing that cotton traceability requires brands to know the farmers who grow it. Even with certified cotton backed by transaction certificates, tracing the fiber back through the supply chain took hours of painstaking investigation.
Gins pay farmers or intermediaries for cotton and hold essential origin data, but their records often lack a standardized format unless they operate within a certified cotton system. Without standardized gin data, information rarely travels downstream, forcing brands to undertake large-scale, unrealistic investigations to trace cotton to its source. The report recommends that brands build lasting relationships with farming communities and the wider network of field workers, input suppliers, agronomists and local traders to obtain full traceability.
“Farmers don’t operate in isolation,” Anne Oudard, former designer and lead of sourcing and supply chain at Cotton Diaries said.
“The information doesn’t get passed on, and so when at the end of the supply chain you want to retrieve this information, you have to go through a massive investigation that is unrealistic at scale,” Anne Oudard, former designer and lead of sourcing and supply chain at Cotton Diaries said.
The #WhoMadeMyCotton investigation started five years ago to map the origins of cotton used in denim, and this report marks its fourth step. The project relies on field visits and conversations in Brazil, India and Turkey to gather insights.
Source: WWD (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/sj-denim/who-made-your-cotton-1239319748)

item.title: Evans Transportation warns excess 3PL use drives up freight rates
item.description:
Evans Transportation, which serves roughly 300 customers, warned that shippers relying on multiple third‑party logistics providers for the same lane may see carriers delay loads and push rates up. He noted that Gulf Coast load‑to‑truck ratios have reached hundreds of loads per truck, a condition that could worsen with an approaching tropical storm.
Conrad described the phenomenon as “broker poker,” explaining that when many 3PLs bid on the same lane carriers learn to hold out for higher payments. He said Evans Transportation retains other 3PLs only when a shipper already has a vetted partner on a given segment, rather than displacing long‑standing relationships. The firm’s managed transportation model combines proprietary technology, off‑the‑shelf tools and an agentic AI voice system that fields initial inbound calls before passing them to live staff.
“Those brokers who are going out to the marketplace over and over and over again on the same lane, they’re driving the rate up because the carriers get smart and they say, I’m going to wait for a little while because you guys are all bidding on it,” John Conrad, Chief Revenue Officer at Evans Transportation Services said.
Evans Transportation describes its managed transportation approach as “outsourcing done right,” combining proprietary technology with off‑the‑shelf tools and, most recently, an agentic AI voice system to handle initial inbound call volume. The company, founded in 1985 and privately held, serves roughly 300 customers and holds an MC number beginning with 1.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/why-adding-3pls-can-backfire-on-shippers)

item.title: Hurricane Isaias threatens Gulf refineries as it nears Category 3 strength
item.description:
Hurricane Isaias, currently a Category 1 storm, is forecast to reach Category 3 with winds up to 100 mph before making landfall Friday around 2 p.m., threatening Gulf Coast refineries and ports. Gulf State refineries in the storm’s path represent half of the nation’s refining capacity, or 18.2 million barrels per day.
Tender rejections in New Orleans, Mobile, and Montgomery are already running between 17% and 19%, above national averages, as shippers move freight ahead of the storm. Rainfall of 3 to 6 inches is expected across the region, with isolated totals possibly reaching 10 inches, raising flood concerns for inland routes. The Ports of Mobile and New Orleans lie in the projected impact zone, while FEMA staging sites in Jacksonville and Atlanta could spur emergency freight demand after landfall.
“I do not play about the weather,” Malcolm Harris, who provided the meteorological analysis said.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/hurricane-isaias-category-3-threat-to-gulf-supply-chain)

item.title: OFAC warns CFOs that sanctions risk can lurk in payment routes
item.description:
On Monday (Oct. 5), the Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control warned foreign financial institutions that continuing to transact with sanctioned entities could expose them to sanctions at any time without notice. The warning came as global supply chain pressures reached a four‑month high, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York’s GSCPI released Tuesday (Oct. 6).
OFAC pointed to recent actions against banks that gave sanctioned actors such as Iran access to correspondent banking and the international financial system. Specifically, the agency cited its August move to cut U.S. correspondent banking access for Banque Misr UAE, its September designation of Turkey‑based Golden Global Bank and its subsidiaries, and its action against Russia’s VTB Bank for Iranian sanctions evasion. Correspondent banking lets a regional bank without direct currency access move money through a partner institution, a link that can become blocked if the intermediary is sanctioned.
“The term ‘cross‑border’ signifies that a payment traverses different legal entities, jurisdictions, regulatory frameworks, sanction regimes,” Emanuela Saccarola, Citi’s head of cross-border payments and services said.
Traditional sanctions controls are heavily counterparty-centric: Who are we paying? Who owns the business? Is the company or its beneficial owner sanctioned? Is the destination permitted. The implication is bigger than freezing the assets of a sanctioned company.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/cross-border-payments/2026/ofac-warning-shows-cfos-sanctions-risk-can-hide-in-the-payment-route)
